{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABYk2ppA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhCJwbQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 29, "title": "Redesign the PC-VAN terminal UI and simulate progressive modem-era text rendering", "body": "## Problem

The browser application currently resembles a dark web form more than a convincing text terminal. The command input, status and AI/storage/offline controls are visually fragmented, and terminal output appears all at once. This undermines the intended nostalgic experience of connecting to PC-VAN.

## Expected outcome

Deliver one coherent, readable, keyboard-first terminal experience with a dominant CRT-inspired display, integrated prompt and tasteful optional visual effects. Add configurable progressive output that approximates the *perceived* arrival of text over a historical modem connection while preserving the exact original transcript, usability and existing application behavior.

## Context

- Existing code: `src/style.css` sets a plain dark bordered terminal and vertically stacked controls; `src/terminal.ts` renders a `<pre class="output">` and separate `<form class="command-form">`. Its `append(...text)` immediately appends all text as one DOM text node. `src/main.ts` wires the terminal to connection, forum, AI, IndexedDB and offline controls. Reinspect the current `main` before implementation.
- **Historical authenticity:** 1996-era PC-VAN menu labels, navigation, and evidence categories remain authoritative from `data/pcvan/` and `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md`. CRT glow, monochrome green/amber/white, decorative bezel, scanlines and any displayed baud rate are **optional presentation reconstructions**, not authenticated PC-VAN screenshots. Do not change historical menu content or invent commands.
- Visual inspiration, not historical evidence: [xterm.js](https://xtermjs.org/) (terminal layout, cursor, keyboard handling); [Horizon BBS](https://www.horizonbbs.org/) (BBS experience); [CRT Terminal Portfolio](https://github.com/atmozki/CRT-terminal-portfolio) (subtle CRT shell/effects). Avoid copying proprietary assets or adopting unrelated ANSI BBS commands.
- A real modem serial line transmits **bits/bytes**, not Unicode characters at a fixed rate. For a nominal 8N1 connection, 300/1200/2400/9600 bps correspond to ~30/120/240/960 serial bytes per second before overhead. Japanese encoding and terminal control sequences affect visible character rate. This app has no modem, so clearly label this a simulation; choose and document a deterministic display-cost model (e.g. Shift_JIS byte lengths for representable characters with explicit fallback) without corrupting Unicode text.
- Preserve existing no-backend operation, WebLLM generation, IndexedDB data, JSON backup, offline caching and GitHub Pages project subpath `/pcvan/`. The change is UI/rendering only; do not introduce xterm.js, a new app framework, remote fonts, large images or unnecessary dependencies without a demonstrated need.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md). New Issue/PR/documentation text is English; the Japanese product UI remains Japanese.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Redesign the page so the terminal transcript and command prompt dominate the viewport on desktop and mobile. Use a cohesive terminal bezel/header/status strip with clear visual hierarchy; move secondary AI, user, storage and offline controls into compact, accessible collapsible settings sections or an equivalent low-distraction arrangement. All existing actions must remain discoverable and operable.
- [ ] Make command entry appear as the terminal's final prompt row, rather than a visually separate generic form, while preserving the existing input, IME-safe Enter submission, command history, keyboard scrolling, focus visibility and screen-reader labels. Never allow a simulated cursor to obscure the real input caret.
- [ ] Provide readable selectable monospace Japanese output preserving exact spaces, newlines, half/full-width characters and long-line horizontal scrolling. Ensure two-column menus remain aligned and the transcript remains usable at narrow viewport widths without clipping commands.
- [ ] Provide coherent selectable visual themes (at least neutral white, green phosphor and amber) with subtle, optional glow/scanline styling. Effects must not compromise text contrast or selection. Treat them as reconstructed aesthetics, not evidence of a specific PC-VAN terminal.
- [ ] Add progressive output to the existing terminal append pipeline with a bounded queue and batched `requestAnimationFrame` (or comparably efficient) rendering; output appears in original order without dropping or duplicating text, even when commands, reconnect output and async AI activity overlap. Do not run a DOM mutation per character or block the command controller.
- [ ] Provide user-selectable nominal modes `300`, `1200`, `2400`, `9600 bps` and `Instant`. Document the mapping from nominal line speed to simulated display timing, including Japanese multi-byte text and an explicit Unicode fallback. Default to a usable retro mode (suggest 2400 bps) and keep Instant easily available. Displayed bps values must be labeled as a simulation, not actual connectivity.
- [ ] Allow a user to reveal all currently queued text immediately (with a visible skip affordance and a keyboard-accessible action), without canceling the underlying session or losing later output. A new command during animation must not create misleading out-of-order text; document and test the chosen flush/queue behavior.
- [ ] Persist the selected theme, speed and effects preference in the existing browser-local settings storage, surviving reload and JSON export/import where appropriate; use the current storage versioning/validation conventions and do not discard existing users' data or require a server.
- [ ] Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by defaulting to non-animated output/effects when requested, while still allowing an explicit user preference. Avoid excessive `aria-live` announcements during character streaming; announce complete logical output appropriately.
- [ ] Preserve full transcript integrity independent of animation: the `端末ログを保存 (.txt)` action exports **all logical output already accepted**, including queued-but-not-yet-painted text, with original newlines, and does not include unsent drafts. Selection/copy of already visible text still works.
- [ ] Add automated tests using the existing Playwright/test setup for display order, queue flushing/skip, mode changes, Japanese Unicode, command submission during animation, transcript download, persisted settings, reduced motion, responsive layout and unchanged forum/navigation flows. Use fake time/controlled frames where suitable; no real WebGPU, modem, model downloads or hosted deployment required.
- [ ] Update README/appropriate docs with controls, accessibility, simulated timing, optional themes, historical caveats and any intentional limitations. Run `npm test`, build and applicable whitespace/link checks; record actual results in the PR.

## Optional validation

Manual nostalgic-feel review on desktop/mobile, including 1990s-like CRT display aesthetics, is welcome but not a mandatory approval gate. Optional real-device/browser visual inspection can inform follow-up changes.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. The changes are client-side and can be tested against the built app before merge. If the repository's existing GitHub Pages workflow deploys after merge, its publication may be observed separately, but hosted publication is not a completion gate for this UI Issue.
